# 1 Samuel Chapter 11 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 188 | **Source Image:** 1SA_011_page_001.jpg, 1SA_011_page_002.jpg

---

**11:1** And-went-up Nahash the-Ammonite and-encamped against Yavesh-gilead. And-said all [the]-men of-Yavesh to Nahash, "Cut for-us a-covenant and-we-will-serve you."

**11:2** And-said to-them Nahash the-Ammonite, "In-this I-will-cut [a covenant] for-you: in-gouging-out for-you every right eye, and-I-will-set it [as] a-reproach upon all Israel."

**11:3** And-said to-him [the]-elders of-Yavesh, "Leave-us-alone seven days, and-we-will-send messengers in-all [the]-territory of-Israel, and-if there-is-no-one saving us, then-we-will-come-out to-you."

**11:4** And-came the-messengers [to] Gibeah of-Saul, and-they-spoke the-words in-[the]-ears of-the-people. And-lifted-up all the-people their-voice and-wept.

**11:5** And-behold, Saul [was]-coming after the-oxen from the-field. And-said Saul, "What [is wrong with] the-people that they-weep?" And-they-recounted to-him the-words of-[the]-men of-Yavesh.

**11:6** And-rushed [the]-spirit of-God upon Saul when-he-heard these words, and-his-anger burned exceedingly.

**11:7** And-he-took a-yoke of-oxen and-cut-them-in-pieces, and-sent [them] in-all [the]-territory of-Israel by-[the]-hand of-the-messengers, saying, "Whoever is-not going-out after Saul and-after Samuel, thus shall-be-done to-his-oxen." And-fell [the]-dread of-YHWH upon the-people, and-they-went-out as-one man.

**11:8** And-he-mustered-them in-Bezek, and-[the]-sons of-Israel were three-hundred thousand, and-[the]-men of-Judah thirty thousand.

**11:9** And-they-said to-the-messengers who-came, "Thus shall-you-say to-[the]-men of-Yavesh-gilead: 'Tomorrow there-will-be deliverance for-you when-the-sun is-hot.'" And-came the-messengers and-told [the]-men of-Yavesh, and-they-were-glad.

**11:10** And-said [the]-men of-Yavesh, "Tomorrow we-will-come-out to-you, and-you-shall-do to-us according-to-all the-good in-your-eyes."

**11:11** And-it-was on-the-next-day, and-Saul put the-people [in] three companies, and-they-came into-[the]-midst of-the-camp in-[the]-morning watch, and-they-struck Ammon until the-heat of-the-day. And-it-was [that] the-ones-remaining were-scattered, and-not were-left among-them two together.

**11:12** And-said the-people to Samuel, "Who [is] the-one-saying, 'Shall-Saul reign over-us?' Give the-men and-we-will-put-them-to-death."

**11:13** And-said Saul, "Not shall-be-put-to-death a-man on-this day, for today YHWH has-made deliverance in-Israel."

**11:14** And-said Samuel to the-people, "Come and-let-us-go [to] the-Gilgal, and-let-us-renew there the-kingship."

**11:15** And-went all the-people [to] the-Gilgal, and-they-made-king there Saul before YHWH in-the-Gilgal, and-they-sacrificed there sacrifices of-peace-offerings before YHWH. And-rejoiced there Saul and-all [the]-men of-Israel exceedingly.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

1. **11:1 -- "Yavesh-gilead"** (יָבֵשׁ גִּלְעָד): The Leningrad Codex spells this as two words. Yavesh means "dry" -- the city name itself. Gilead is the regional designation east of the Jordan.

2. **11:2 -- "gouging out every right eye"** (בִּנְקוֹר לָכֶם כָּל־עֵין יָמִין): The verb נקר (to gouge, bore out) is in the infinitive construct. This mutilation would render warriors unable to fight, since shields covered the left eye.

3. **11:6 -- "rushed the spirit of God"** (וַתִּצְלַח רוּחַ אֱלֹהִים): The verb צלח (to rush upon) is the same used of the Spirit's empowerment of Samson (Judges 14:6, 19; 15:14). The parallel deliberately connects Saul's charismatic leadership to the judge tradition.

4. **11:7 -- "dread of YHWH"** (פַּחַד יְהוָה): The Leningrad Codex reads "dread of YHWH" -- a divinely induced terror that compels obedience, not mere fear of Saul.

5. **11:8 -- Troop count**: The Leningrad Codex reads three hundred thousand for Israel and thirty thousand for Judah. The separate counting of Judah is noteworthy, anticipating the later division of the monarchy.

6. **11:15 -- "they made king"** (וַיַּמְלִכוּ): This is Saul's second coronation -- a "renewal" (חדש) of the kingship as Samuel says in v.14. The Gilgal location connects to Joshua's original entry into the land.

-- EMET
